extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature; scientists and scientifically literate public
extracted.subtask_description: Summarising, evaluating, and reporting recent scientific papers, museum/field reports, and institutional news for a general scientific-audience magazine (Nature). Emphasises clear presentation, judgement of evidence, and concise reporting of methods/results/implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type A — Response of eyeless forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of phototropic responses for eyeless animals labelled 'Type A. Response of eyeless forms.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original text guidance: '— Usually negative; sometimes positive, and then usually to very weak light. Response to intensity. Response to definite objects in the visual field. — Not simple reactions; responses involve psychical phenomena. Respond (1) to moving objects; (2) to stationary objects.' (presented by Mr. Cole as part of his classification). Use these behavioural criteria (positive/negative phototropism, sensitivity to intensity, response to definite objects, and distinction between responses to moving vs. stationary objects) to characterise and classify eyeless phototropic responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative wood sampling for description/report
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for selecting specimens of new woods for description or report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original guidance: 'He attaches special value to cylindrical samples with a dome-shaped top as showing even variation of grain from the radial to the quarter.' Use cylindrical samples with a domed top to capture representative variation of grain (radial to quarter) when preparing specimens for description or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of evidence for extraordinary claims (sthenometer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard for accepting novel/mechanistic claims about instruments or phenomena (example: claims of an 'unknown nerve force' from the sthenometer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the review: because Stratton & Phillips showed heat radiation causes the observed motion, 'Much more substantial evidence will be required than that adduced in the article ... before any firm foundation can be secured for the position taken up by Dr. Schofield.' Guidance: require controlled experiments, alternative-explanation elimination (e.g., heat/radiation controls), replication, and quantitative measures (e.g., thermopile correlation) before endorsing novel causal claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and content standards for rainfall maps (isohyets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for maps accompanying meteorological volumes: clarity and depiction of rainfall by equal-amount lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The maps which accompany the volume are very clear, and exhibit the rainfall for the year 1906 by lines showing equal amounts (isohyets) ; the amounts on the west coast ... range from 1200 mm. to 3000 mm.' Guidance: produce clear maps, show isohyets to visualise spatial rainfall distribution, and annotate ranges/values for regions of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for meteorological dataset reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended content and scope for published rainfall/meteorological statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As practised by the Meteorological Institute: include observations from a large network (the report deals with about 427 rainfall stations and summaries for 507 stations), provide daily observations for many places (200), daily snowfall statistics for ~50 places, and monthly/yearly summaries with historical means (in some cases back to 1867). Include clear maps and comprehensive summaries to support analysis and comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-precision atomic-weight determination methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and methodological criteria for gravimetric determination of atomic weights (illustrated by Prof. T. W. Richards' work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original methods/guidance: determine potassium atomic weight by ascertaining ratio of weight of potassium chloride to that of silver chloride produced using almost exactly theoretical silver nitrate; use a Gooch crucible with a platinum-sponge matting to determine silver haloid weight with high accuracy; introduce corrections for minute retained silver chloride in mother liquors; cross-check with different halides (KBr → AgBr). Apply many refinements, report uncertainties, and consider implications for other atomic weights (e.g., nitrogen) when selecting reference values for silver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological map publication conventions (editions and scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for issuing geological maps in multiple editions and an appropriate scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original guidance: issue two editions—a 'solid' edition omitting glacial deposits and a 'drift' edition indicating such deposits by colour. Use a clear, conventional scale (example given: 1 inch to the mile) and colour printing to distinguish deposits/features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbit determination and handling of residuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards when publishing orbital elements: reconciling observed vs. calculated positions and explaining discrepancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Prof. Doberck's re-investigation of α Centauri: if elements do not represent measured angles, re-investigate using more observations; where differences between observed and calculated positions remain, account for them by (a) unusually large constant errors in measures or (b) presence of an unseen third body. Publish revised elements and supply an accompanying ephemeris for the stated interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for describing new taxa/assemblages
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for papers describing new genera/species (illustrated by crinoid descriptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe distinctive morphological characters (e.g., acorn-like calyx, broad spaces between radials with leathery skin), give geographic provenance (Japanese waters, Queen Charlotte group), compare with related taxa, and discuss taxonomic/familial implications (e.g., may indicate a family by itself). Provide illustrations/plates and explicit diagnostic features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional adequacy indicators for college/science departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria used to evaluate a college's scientific capacity and needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess laboratory/experimental equipment, library resources (noting annual purchase funds; original text: 'only about £10 a year is available for the purchase of books'), availability of teaching staff and departments (agriculture, electrical engineering, fisheries), and specialised schools (e.g., forestry). Note where limited resources constrain efficiency and highlight areas needing funding or apparatus to reach 'maximum efficiency.'
